options: An animal that hunts and eats other animals
An animal that eats only plants
A living thing that makes its own food
questions.explanation: A predator hunts, catches, and eats other animals - it gets its energy from prey.
questions.misconception: Predators eat animals they catch; plant-eaters are herbivores, not predators.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a predator?
questions.explanation: A wolf hunts and eats other animals, making it a predator.
questions.misconception: Rabbits and deer eat plants - they are prey for predators, not predators themselves.

questions.prompt: Which helps a predator catch its food?
questions.explanation: Speed, sharp senses, claws, and teeth all help predators catch prey.
questions.misconception: Predators are built to hunt - speed and weaponry beat slow, armored bodies for catching food.

questions.prompt: Why do predators matter to an ecosystem?
options: They keep prey populations from growing too large
They scare away all other animals
questions.explanation: By eating prey, predators keep prey numbers in balance so they do not overuse resources.
questions.misconception: Predators control population sizes - removing them lets prey boom and damage their own food supply.
